archetype.name: Retooling (offense in collapse)
archetype.definition: A team two years removed from a 14-win season whose offense has bottomed out behind a struggling line and a three-man quarterback carousel, leaving a middling defense to keep games respectable.

report.headline: A broken offense and a quarterback carousel have sunk a recent contender.
report.take:
Philadelphia arrives at Week 12 at 3-7 and last in the NFC East. These are the Eagles of 14 wins in 2024 and 11 last year. The offense is the wreckage. It ranks last in yards per game (260.7) and last in success rate (36.2%), 30th in points per game and 30th in offensive EPA. Three different quarterbacks have started. Jalen Hurts opened the year and hasn't started since Week 7. Tanner McKee and Joe Milton III have taken the starts since, and the passing game has cratered with them: -9.5 passing EPA in the loss at Washington and -13.3 against the Giants.

The line explains as much as the quarterbacks. Philadelphia has the league's worst stuff rate (29.8% of runs stopped at or behind the line), 2.1 yards before contact (29th) and 3.16 yards a carry (30th). It has also allowed 30 sacks, 30th in the league. When the run game can't stay ahead of the chains and the quarterback is under siege, a team ends up with the league's 31st-ranked time of possession. That puts a defense that was ninth in EPA last year on the field far too long. The defense has slid to 26th in EPA allowed and dead last in takeaways with 4. The opportunistic, plus-turnover identity of 2024 and 2025 is gone.

The record does flatter how bad the luck has been. The point differential implies 5.1 wins, and the Eagles sit at -2.1 wins over expected, 31st in the league. They lost one-score games to the Rams and Jaguars and covered the spread in only 11.1% of games. Don't mistake that for a hidden good team, though. Net EPA ranks 31st, so the play has been bottom-two even if the scoreboard has been a little crueler than it should be. This is a bad team that has also been somewhat unlucky, not a good team being robbed.

Where it goes from here depends almost entirely on the quarterback spot and health. The 19-16 win over Pittsburgh came out of a bye and was built on defense: five sacks and 73 rushing yards allowed. That is the template for what this roster can do, which is grind low-scoring games and hope the offense avoids giveaways. The schedule has two soft spots in Arizona and Indianapolis, both 3-8. It then closes with Seattle, Houston, San Francisco and the Giants, so a late surge into relevance is unlikely.

strengths.title: Defense bends more than it breaks
strengths.body: Despite a low EPA rank and an offense that gives it no rest, the defense allows 24.6 points a game, 18th, and a 57.6% red-zone touchdown rate, 14th. It has also limited deep shots well, 12th in deep EPA allowed. That kept early-season losses to the Rams and Jaguars within one score. The depth is being tested now, with Zack Baun on IR, so this is the strength most at risk.

strengths.title: Pass rush has woken up lately
strengths.body: For most of the year the pressure numbers have been poor: 18.2% pressure rate (26th) and 30th in QB hit rate. The last two games broke that pattern, with six sacks against the Giants and five against Pittsburgh. Both of those offenses rank in the middle of the league or lower, so treat it as a hopeful sign rather than a new identity.

strengths.title: Aggressive on fourth down
strengths.body: Sirianni leads the league in fourth-down go rate. It is the right call for an offense that struggles to finish drives with field goals or explosive plays. Special teams sit mid-pack at 15th in EPA per game, so the hidden yardage isn't costing them either. It's a small edge that will persist as long as the coaching approach does.

concerns.title: The line loses at the point of attack
concerns.body: The run game is last in stuff rate and 30th in yards per carry, and backs are getting barely two yards before contact. Running has gone nowhere even with Saquon Barkley carrying most of the load. Pass protection is no better, with 30 sacks allowed, 30th, and a 8.5% sack rate. That is a structural problem that a quarterback change can't fix, and it has persisted through all three starters.

concerns.title: Quarterback play has fallen apart
concerns.body: Hurts' early games produced positive passing EPA against Washington and Tennessee. Since then the passing game has posted deep negatives with every starter. The worst came in Milton's debut against the Giants: -13.3 passing EPA and seven sacks taken. The offense is last in success rate. With McKee questionable with a rib injury and no clear answer, this will likely define the rest of the year.

concerns.title: The turnover edge has vanished
concerns.body: The Eagles ranked 2nd in turnover differential in 2024 and 6th in 2025. They're now 28th, with the league's fewest takeaways and a season turnover differential of -5. Takeaways are partly luck and could tick up. Still, a defense ranked 30th in QB hit rate doesn't force many hurried throws, so expect only modest improvement.

trend.note: They opened 2-0 without covering either game, then lost every week from late September into November as the quarterback job changed hands. The grinding win over Pittsburgh out of the bye is the only break in that slide so far.

nextGame.headline: Short-week rematch in Dallas against an offense that ran them over
nextGame.body:
Dallas has a top-tier offense, third in EPA per play and fourth both passing and rushing, paired with the league's worst defense by EPA. Philadelphia has the reverse problem: an offense 29th in EPA per play and a defense 25th. In Week 7 the Cowboys won 38-21 in Philadelphia and ran for 204 yards. Now the Eagles go to Dallas on four days' rest. The Book has Dallas -8.5 with a 47.5 total, and Philadelphia is +361 on the moneyline.

Availability tilts things further. McKee (ribs) is questionable, and Milton has started the last two games. Barkley (neck, illness) and Dallas Goedert (shin) are both limited and questionable. Dontayvion Wicks and Zack Baun are on IR, so the middle of the defense loses its every-down linebacker. Quinyon Mitchell left the Pittsburgh game with a hamstring injury and is questionable, and Jonathan Jones didn't practice, so the corner room is thin against a top-five passing offense. Dallas has its own holes. Starting guard Tyler Booker and tight end Jake Ferguson are out. DaRon Bland is on IR, safeties Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke are out, and linebacker Jaishawn Barham is out while Dee Winters is questionable. That leaves a weak defense even thinner at the second and third levels.

waysToWin.title: Feed the top receiver downfield
waysToWin.body: Dallas has been the league's worst defense against opposing WR1s, giving up 6.8 PPR points a game over their average. It is 30th in pass EPA allowed, and both starting safeties are out. Whoever starts at quarterback has to get the ball to Makai Lemon or DeVonta Smith early and often. This is the one matchup where the Eagles' talent clearly outclasses what's across from it.

waysToWin.title: Live on third and fourth down
waysToWin.body: Dallas allows conversions on 48.3% of third downs, worst in the league, and the Eagles go for it on fourth more than anyone. Long, methodical drives would shorten the game, keep Dak Prescott on the sideline and make the 8.5-point spread more manageable. It is the only realistic script for an offense this inefficient.

waysToWin.title: Keep the sack surge going
waysToWin.body: The front has 11 sacks over the last two games. Dallas has protected well, with the 5th-best sack rate allowed, but it is playing without starting guard Booker. A couple of drive-killing sacks on a short week is how a 2-point-per-game underdog defense steals possessions.

waysToLose.title: Dallas runs it down their throat again
waysToLose.body: The Cowboys ran for 204 yards in the first meeting. Their rushing offense ranks 4th in EPA, and Philadelphia's run defense ranks 31st in EPA allowed and now loses Baun. If Dallas stays on schedule on early downs, the Eagles' defense won't get the passing downs where its pass rush has started to show up.

waysToLose.title: No run game, then a pass-rush avalanche
waysToLose.body: Dallas is 2nd-stingiest against opposing lead backs by EPA per play, and the Eagles have the league's worst stuff rate. A questionable Barkley makes it worse. If the run game stalls, a young quarterback faces obvious passing downs behind a line that has given up the 25th-worst sack rate. That is how Week 9's seven-sack loss to the Giants happened.

waysToLose.title: A shootout they can't match
waysToLose.body: The 47.5 total points toward Dallas scoring freely. Prescott's passing offense ranks 4th in EPA, while Philadelphia's secondary is 24th in pass EPA allowed and possibly without Mitchell. An offense 30th in points per game can't trade touchdowns, so an early two-score deficit ends this.

nextGame.watch: Dallas' early-down runs against a front missing Baun. If the Eagles can't hold up better than they did in the 204-yard first meeting, nothing else matters.

restOfSeason.body:
Some of the record is bad luck. The differential implies about five wins, and close losses to the Rams and Jaguars could have gone the other way. Expect a little positive regression in close games and takeaways, since nobody stays last in takeaways forever. What won't regress on its own is the line and the quarterback play. Those are the core of a bottom-two efficiency team, and nothing in the dossier suggests a fix is coming. Baun's projected mid-December return and better health at running back and tight end would help at the margins.

The schedule offers two winnable games right after Dallas, at Arizona and home against Indianapolis. Arizona's defense ranks 31st, a rare chance for this offense to move the ball. Seattle and San Francisco are a different class, and Houston and the Giants are tougher than they look. A realistic finish is two or three more wins, low-scoring games throughout, and an offseason spent on the quarterback room and the interior line.

confidence.note: Ten games of consistently poor efficiency, but the QB situation is unsettled.
